ddl:
CREATE TABLE College (
    College_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    College_Location VARCHAR(255),
    College_Name VARCHAR(255),
    Total_Number_of_Staff INTEGER,
    Total_Number_of_Students INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE Student (
    Age INTEGER,
    Associated_College_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Date_of_Birth DATETIME,
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Registration_Time DATETIME,
    Student_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Telephone INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Associated_College_ID) REFERENCES College(College_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Teacher (
    Age INTEGER,
    Associated_College_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Contact_Information VARCHAR(255),
    Gender VARCHAR(255),
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Teacher_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Associated_College_ID) REFERENCES College(College_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Course (
    Class_Hours FLOAT,
    Classroom INTEGER,
    Course_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Course_Summary VARCHAR(255),
    Credit_Number FLOAT,
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Teaching_Teacher_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Teaching_Teacher_ID) REFERENCES Teacher(Teacher_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Course_Enrollment_and_Grade (
    Course_Grade INTEGER,
    Course_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Enrollment_Time DATETIME,
    Student_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Student_ID, Course_ID, Enrollment_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Course_ID) REFERENCES Course(Course_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Student_ID) REFERENCES Student(Student_ID)
);
gold_question: Academic administration system business requirement description: The school has multiple colleges, each with a college name, college location, total number of staff, and total number of students. Each college consists of multiple students and teachers. Each student has a Student ID, name, gender, date of birth, age, telephone, registration time, and associated college ID. Each teacher has a Teacher ID, gender, name, age, contact information, title, and associated college ID. The school offers multiple courses, each with a Course ID, name, credit number, teaching Teacher ID, course summary, class hours, and classroom. Students can enroll in multiple courses, and each enrollment requires recording the Student ID, Course ID, enrollment time, and course grade.
nl_text:
The database schema named 'rschema_0338' contains five tables: College, Student, Teacher, Course, and Course_Enrollment_and_Grade.
The College table represents the main entity in the system, holding information about each college, including its unique ID, location, name, number of staff, and number of students. The College_ID is the primary key for this table.
The Student table is a more detailed entity, storing information about each student, including their age, associated college ID, date of birth, gender, name, registration time, student ID, and telephone number. The Associated_College_ID is a foreign key referencing the College_ID in the College table, ensuring data integrity and referential integrity.
The Teacher table also holds information about each teacher, including their age, associated college ID, contact information, gender, name, teacher ID, and title. The Associated_College_ID is a foreign key referencing the College_ID in the College table.
The Course table represents the courses offered by the colleges. It holds information about each course, including class hours, classroom, course ID, course summary, credit number, name, and the ID of the teacher teaching the course. The Teaching_Teacher_ID is a foreign key referencing the Teacher_ID in the Teacher table.
Finally, the Course_Enrollment_and_Grade table represents the enrollment and grades of students in different courses. It holds information about each enrollment, including course grade, course ID, enrollment time, and student ID. The Course_ID and Student_ID are foreign keys referencing the Course_ID and Student_ID in their respective tables respectively, ensuring data integrity and referential integrity. The combination of Student_ID, Course_ID, and Enrollment_Time forms the primary key of this table, ensuring entity integrity.
